subject: Request: short-term capacity bridge for upcoming campaign — billing & terms
messages:
From: Emma Stone <emma@nimbushealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Nathan Lee <nathan.lee@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Need short-term capacity for Sept campaign — estimate and billing questions

Hi Vivek,

Quick ask — we have a time-limited digital outreach campaign scheduled for the first two weeks of September. Based on our preliminary forecast, we expect a ~3x spike in inference volume for a 10-day window versus our current committed throughput.

Two questions: 1) can Redwood provide a short-term capacity increase / temporary tier for that window, and 2) how will overage be invoiced — can we get a blended rate or a capped surcharge instead of full pay-as-you-go?

We can share the usage profile (attached) and want to avoid unexpected invoices. Also open to a short-term committed uplift if that helps with rate fairness.

Thanks — Emma
Emma Stone
Head of Product, Nimbus Health
emma@nimbushealth.com

Attachment: nimbus_usage_report_may2026.csv (CSV — 1.2MB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Emma Stone <emma@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Nathan Lee <nathan.lee@nimbushealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Need short-term capacity for Sept campaign — estimate and billing questions

Hi Emma — thanks for the note and the usage file. Appreciate the heads-up. We can absolutely support a short, predictable uplift — two pragmatic paths we usually propose: 

1) Temporary capacity bridge: reserve a capped additional throughput for the campaign window. We apply a blended surcharge on the incremental units (lower than PAYG) and amortize a portion as a credit if you decide to migrate the uplift into a longer commit within 60 days.

2) Short-term committed uplift: a one-month committed increase at a discounted committed rate; lower unit price but requires a short-term commitment and invoice adjustment.

Initial recommendation based on your profile: option (1) — it preserves flexibility and limits near-term cash commitment. Ill loop in Marissa (sales lead) and Ben (finance) to draft a 1-page "capacity bridge" term sheet. If you can confirm exact campaign window and a conservative peak multiplier well put numbers to it.

Proposed next steps: 
- Emma/Nathan confirm campaign dates (start/end) and expected peak multiplier by EOD 8/28.
- Redwood to send capacity-bridge term sheet and estimated invoice impact by 8/29.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

[Please see attached: draft process — will follow with formal term sheet (PDF)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 15:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Need short-term capacity for Sept campaign — estimate and billing questions

Vivek / Ben — I ran a quick simulation against Nimbus's May profile (thanks Emma) and a 3x short window gives ~2.9M incremental tokens over 10 days. Under our standard PAYG they'd see ~$4.2k of incremental charges.

Proposal (capacity-bridge-v1):
- 10-day capped uplift (2026-09-01 through 2026-09-10) with a blended incremental rate 30% below PAYG for the uplifted units.
- If Nimbus converts the uplift into a 3-month commit within 60 days, Redwood will apply a credit equal to 25% of the uplift surcharge toward the commit (applied retroactively to the uplift invoice).
- If they exceed the capped uplift during the window, overages revert to standard PAYG for the excess beyond the cap.

I've attached a 1-page term sheet draft (capacity-bridge-term-sheet-v1.pdf). Ben — can you confirm we can amortize credit on our side (simple invoice credit) and that the blended rate is acceptable from a margin perspective?

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Sales Director, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachment: capacity-bridge-term-sheet-v1.pdf (PDF — 48KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Stone <emma@nimbushealth.com>, Nathan Lee <nathan.lee@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Need short-term capacity for Sept campaign — estimate and billing questions

Hi all — reviewed the numbers and the proposed credit flow. Finance approves the capacity-bridge-v1 structure with the following clarifications: 

- Blended incremental rate = PAYG * 0.7 (as proposed). We'll include a line-item that shows the PAYG equivalent and the applied discount for transparency.
- Credit mechanics: if Nimbus converts to a commit within 60 days, we will issue an invoice credit equal to 25% of the uplift surcharge. That credit will be applied on the month following conversion.
- Billing cadence: uplift will be invoiced in the normal monthly invoice (September), with any conversion credit applied in the next invoice cycle.
- Legal: term sheet is non-binding. If Nimbus wants to proceed, I'll ask Legal to produce a short amendment to the Master Services Agreement covering the cap and credit mechanism.

Emma — if that matches what you need, please reply with a one-line confirmation of the campaign window and well send the final PDF and a HubSpot activity.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
